biggest_catch: The points have no fixed cash value: 50,000 Rapid Rewards points are worth roughly $625-$650 in Southwest flights at the program's typical value (about 1.25 cents per point), and you can only use them on Southwest. Year-one math: about $625 in flight value minus the $99 annual fee leaves roughly $526 net in the first year. Only claim this if you were already going to spend $1,000 in 3 months on normal purchases; never spend extra to hit the target. Chase and Southwest's official restriction: the bonus is available only if you do not have a current Southwest Rapid Rewards personal card and have not received a personal Southwest cardmember bonus in the last 24 months (business cards are excluded from that restriction).
catches: Only claim this if you were already going to spend the money anyway; never spend extra just to hit the $1,000 minimum, because manufactured spending turns a bonus into debt.

Year-one math: 50,000 Rapid Rewards points are worth roughly $625-$650 in Southwest flights at typical program value, minus the $99 annual fee, which leaves about $526 net in the first year. Points are not cash: they can only be spent on Southwest flights, and devaluations or expiration risk are real.

Applying triggers a hard credit inquiry, which typically knocks a few points off your credit score for a short time. Chase also uses its unpublished 5/24 pattern: applicants with five or more newly opened personal cards across any issuer in the last 24 months are generally denied.
This card's APR is around 20% or higher, so carrying a balance would wipe out the bonus fast. Pay the statement balance in full every month or this offer loses you money.

Chase and Southwest's official rule: this product is available to you only if you do not have a current Southwest Rapid Rewards personal credit card and have not received a new personal Southwest cardmember bonus within the last 24 months. This does not apply to Southwest business cards.
Chase's unpublished 5/24 pattern: five or more new personal cards opened in the last 24 months generally means denial, even with excellent credit.

Points post after the qualifying purchases and can take up to 30 days after your statement-cycle date to appear in your Rapid Rewards account; the account must be open and not in default when they post.

steps: Go to the official Chase Southwest Plus page and read the current offer headline and the Pricing & Terms before anything else.
Confirm your eligibility: you do not currently hold a Southwest Rapid Rewards personal card and have not received a personal Southwest cardmember bonus in the last 24 months.
Apply online. Expect a hard credit inquiry.
Use the card for the purchases you were already planning, totaling at least $1,000 in the first 3 months from account opening.
Pay the statement balance in full every month; do not carry a balance at the ~20%+ APR.
Allow up to 30 days after the statement-cycle date for the 50,000 points to appear in your Rapid Rewards account.
Before the second $99 annual fee hits, check whether the card's anniversary points and benefits earned you more than $99 in real value in year one, and downgrade or cancel if not.
timing: Spend $1,000 on purchases in the first 3 months from account opening. Points can take up to 30 days after your statement-cycle date to appear in your Rapid Rewards account.
